# What the duck can do

## About this list

This is the full list of what the duck can do, sorted by kind: how it walks and turns, how it sits and rests, the motions of its trained skill table, its emotions, its reflexes, the commands you can give it, and everything it does on its own.

The list is generated. `tools/motion_list.py` reads the real tables in the code and writes this file and its translation. Run `python tools/motion_list.py` to write them again. Run `python tools/motion_list.py --check` to see if they are up to date; a test fails when they are not. Please do not edit them by hand.

**Status.** Everything here was measured in the MuJoCo simulator (the upstream `robotd --sim`). Nothing has run on a real robot. Read [SAFETY.md](../SAFETY.md) before you try any of it on hardware.

### Counts

| Part | Rows |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Gaits | 8 |
| 2. Posture and rest | 6 |
| 3. Trained motion skills | 30 skills, 19 page buttons |
| 4. Emotions | 14 |
| 5. Reflexes | 13 |
| 6. Commands and tricks | 13 (7 built in, 5 tricks, 1 pointed) |
| 7. Autonomous behaviours | 59 |

The same trained skill can serve several acts, so the parts overlap. The brain has 71 acts in all: 6 in section 2, 6 in section 5 and 59 in section 7.

### Legend

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | What starts it. `autonomous`: the duck's own brain decides. `command`: a person says it (or points). `trick`: taught first, then commanded. `reflex`: an automatic reaction to what the senses feel. `page demo`: a button on the simulator page. |
| **Runs on** | What moves the body. **Walking policy**: Pollen's v5 walking and standing network (`velstand`); standing still is the same network with no walk command. **Sit-stand policy**: Pollen's v5 network for sitting and for standing up. **Trained skill**: a network we trained ourselves, one entry of the motion table (section 3). **Keyframes**: a fixed recording of head, neck, beak and body pitch (Pollen's `microduck_emotions`). **Brain program**: a head, neck and beak program made by the brain on top of the standing (or sit-stand) policy; the legs have no training for it. |
| **Safety** | The rules that limit it: a cap per hour, a minimum gap, the fastest walk it may start from, and the lean after which it is handed back to the walking policy. The guard that checks them is `duckmind.skilltrain.guard`. |
| **Status** | The result of the simulator check, in the page's own words: Passed, Passed with limits or Failed. A dash means it has no check of its own; it is only exercised as part of the whole duck living in the simulator. |
| **Growth day** | The base day from which the act can appear. Each duck's own pace moves it a little. |
| **Walks** | Whether the act steps with the legs (under the walking policy). |
| **Sounds** | The calls it may make while it does the act. “silent” means it may also make none. |

## 1. Gaits

How the duck gets around. Pollen's walking policy walks at 0 m/s or at least 0.30 m/s, and turns only while it steps. So a turn on the spot, a quick turn and a panic run each have their own trained skill (section 3). Speeds and caps come from the code's own constants.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `walk` | Normal walk: forward, with gentle turns while it steps. | 0, or 0.30–0.55 m/s. Turn up to 1.0 rad/s, only while stepping. | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | autonomous; command (`come`, `follow`, `go_home`, `go_there`) | The policy does not step below 0.30 m/s. The cap is 0.55 m/s; no falls were measured up to it in the simulator. | — |
| `approach` | Walking up to one particular thing, such as a toy or a person. | Up to 0.40 m/s. | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | autonomous | A lower cap than a free walk. | — |
| `arc` | Walking in a curve: a sharp turn while it steps. | At least 0.35 m/s in a sharp turn. Turn up to 1.0 rad/s. | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | autonomous | A sharp turn is never slower than 0.35 m/s. | — |
| `back_arc` | Backing up while turning, beside a thing or out of a corner. | -0.40 m/s with a turn of 1.0 rad/s: 0.6 s beside a thing, 1.3 s out of a corner. | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | autonomous | Always an arc, never straight back. The brain backs out of a corner at most 3 times at one place, and only if its memory says there is room behind. | — |
| `reverse` | Backing up straight, only while docking at the nest. | -0.40 to -0.30 m/s straight back. Docking steps forward: 0.30–0.40 m/s. | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | autonomous; command (`go_home`) | The brain's walking rules allow a straight reverse only while docking. Anywhere else it backs up only in an arc (`back_arc`). | — |

| `quick_turn_left`, `quick_turn_right` | Fast turn on the spot. Without the skill the walking policy runs the flight at 0.52–0.55 m/s. | Trained skill `panic_run`; without the skill, the walking policy | autonomous (`flee`, `retreat`) | From standing or a walk of 0.60 m/s or slower. The arc entries `panic_arc_left`, `panic_arc_right` keep their rules, but the live path does not ask for them. | Passed with limits |

## 2. Posture and rest

How the duck sits, stands up and rests. Standing, standing still included, is the walking policy with no walk command. Sitting is Pollen's sit-stand policy. Sitting down and standing up change which of the two runs. The rest acts are brain programs on top of the sitting policy; `sunbathe` first walks into the light.

| Id | Name | What it looks like | Trigger | Posture | Walks | Growth day | Sounds | Runs on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sit_down` | Sit down | slowly lowers and sits down, head relaxed | autonomous, command | standing or sitting | no | 0 | silent, coo~ | Sit-stand policy (Pollen v5) |
| `stand_up` | Stand up | pushes up to stand, and looks up for a moment | autonomous, command | standing or sitting | no | 0 | silent, peep | Sit-stand policy (Pollen v5) |
| `nap` | Nap | dozes off in two or three steps, head tucked low, an occasional twitch | autonomous | sitting (asleep) | no | 0 | silent, peep | Brain program on the sit-stand policy |
| `doze` | Doze | head slowly droops, nods once and lifts again | autonomous | sitting (asleep) | no | 0 | silent | Brain program on the sit-stand policy |
| `rest_sit` | Sit and rest | sits relaxed, head a little low, glancing around now and then | autonomous | sitting | no | 0 | silent, coo~ | Brain program on the sit-stand policy |
| `sunbathe` | Sunbathe | walks into the brightest patch of sunlight on the floor, sits facing the light, head low, face tilted slightly toward the brightness, barely moving (a squinting look: this body has no eyelids) | autonomous | standing or sitting | yes | 0 | silent, coo~ | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) |

## 3. Trained motion skills

The motion table is a set of small neural networks (ONNX files) that we trained ourselves. `robotd` runs one of them for a short time in place of the walking policy, then hands the body back. Each entry has a rule in the guard (`duckmind.skilltrain.guard`):

- **Starts from**: the postures it was tested from. Anything else is refused.
- **Per hour**: the most uses in a rolling hour, against gearbox wear. All skills together: at most 60 an hour.
- **Min gap**: the least time (s) between two uses of the same entry.
- **Walk speed up to**: when it starts from a walk, the fastest walk (m/s) it was tested from. A dash: it starts only from standing or sitting.
- **Tilt abort**: if the body leans past this angle (degrees) while the skill runs, the skill is handed back to the walking policy. “never” means this watch is off: the forward roll turns the body over on purpose.

Three more rules are not skills, so they are not listed: `startle_release` ends a crouch, `bow_release` ends a lie-low, and `skill_abort` hands any running skill back to the walking policy.

A skill starts only when the trunk is upright (under 20°) and still, and the duck is not held, docked or fallen, and no other skill runs. A person pressing a page button skips the wear caps (per hour, gap, total) but never the safety rules. A table made from the strain checks may halve a cap or remove a skill (`caps_from_strain`), so an installed table can be stricter than the numbers here. 7 entries marked with † are not in the installed table, to fit robotd's 30 slots; the picker uses the nearest level instead.

## 4. Emotions

There are 14 emotions, each a short motion of head, neck, beak and body pitch with a sound. The keyframes come from Pollen Robotics' `microduck_emotions` (Apache-2.0, see [THIRD_PARTY.md](../THIRD_PARTY.md)); the sounds are made again in this duck's own voice. On the page the buttons are called `emo_<id>`.

The duck keeps standing for all of them except `devastated` and `play_dead`, which sit down first and stand up after. The brain picks one from its own state and its temperament: each emotion has a cooldown, no emotion starts within 14 s of another ending, and never while it flees, is startled, rights itself, sleeps, docks or runs one of its programs. A reflex, a fall, a lift or sleep ends an emotion at once.

`play_dead` also drives the legs (robotd's `robot.poseJoints`, which only the simulator build has). With the official robotd it can only sit: “A call, the head whips to the side and it sits; the head tilts back, it goes quiet, a last dying call, then it stands up by itself (about 9 s). This simulator's robot program has no 'pose the joints' command, so it only sits and plays dead: it does not lie down or lift its feet.”

## 5. Reflexes

Reflexes are the fast layer under the brain's choices: what the senses feel reaches the body without deliberation, a little different each time (it depends on the size of the stimulus, on arousal, and on habituation: the tenth clap gets a weaker turn of the head). Some reflexes start an act of the same id. `held` and `wheee_ride` are reflex acts with no reflex of their own.

| Id | Reflex | Act it starts | What the act looks like | Set off by | Sounds | Runs on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orient` | Turns to look | — | — | A sudden sound, something moving or new in view, or the lights coming on. | — | Brain program (head, neck, beak) on the standing policy |
| `startle` | Startled | Startled | head jerks back (and its neck pulls in if it's sitting), then it freezes | A sudden loud sound, or something rushing at its face. | silent, Quack quack! (alarm) | Brain program, plus trained skills (families: `startle`, `freeze`, `hop_back`) |
| `freeze` | Holds still | Freeze and stare | head raised a little, staring at one spot without moving | Right after a startle, or when the lights go out. It lasts as long as the fear does. | silent | Brain program, plus trained skills (families: `freeze`) |
| `withdraw` | Pull back | Pull back | pulls its head back and away from the side that was touched | A touch it did not expect, such as a poke. | silent | Brain program (head, neck, beak) on the standing policy; sometimes also a quick step away on the walking policy |
| `lean_in` | Leans in | — | — | A stroke, or a touch it saw coming. | — | Brain program (head, neck, beak) on the standing policy |
| `veer` | Veers away | — | — | Something close ahead, a brush against it, or its own leg or beak meeting something. | — | Walking policy: the walk is stopped or steered |
| `drop_stop` | A drop ahead, stopped | — | — | The floor ahead is missing. | — | Walking policy: the walk is stopped or steered |
| `bump_stop` | Bumped into something, stopped | — | — | It touches something ahead, or a step is blocked. | — | Walking policy: the walk is stopped or steered |
| `righting` | Fell over, getting back up | Get back up | after a fall, lets its body get back up on its own, then shakes its head and looks at its feet | A fall. | Quack quack! (alarm) | Walking policy, then the sit-stand policy on a second try; 60% of the time a `shake_1` follows |
| `lifted` | Feels picked up, stays quiet and still | — | — | Being picked up. | — | Sit-stand policy (it sits when it feels the pick-up) with a quiet brain program |
| `stabilise` | Its body wobbled, so it stopped to steady itself | — | — | The body wobbles or jolts while walking. | — | Walking policy: the walk is stopped or steered |
| `held` | — | Being held | picked up: quiet, head slowly looking around | Being picked up and held. | silent, hm? | Sit-stand policy (it sits when it feels the pick-up) with a quiet brain program |
| `wheee_ride` | — | Wheee~ ride | when picked up and swung, it lifts its head into the wind, beak slightly open, going “wheee~” all the way, and stops when set down | Being picked up and swung. | wheee~ | Sit-stand policy (it sits when it feels the pick-up) with a quiet brain program |

## 6. Commands and tricks

What you can tell the duck. The words people say, in six languages, live in `duckmind.neuro.command_words`; the table shows the first 3 phrases in this file's language. A phrase can sit inside a sentence (“please sit down for me”); a “no” just before it cancels it. The built-in verbs work whenever the duck is awake, not afraid, not held and not in flight. A command asks for an act (“Claims”). The duck can still refuse, for example when it is asleep, afraid, held or low on battery, and the page says why.

`go_there` is not a spoken command: on the page you point at the floor. It is experimental.

**Tricks start locked.** A duck that was never taught a trick still hears it, but only now and then does it by luck (15% of the time). Praise after a trick raises its proficiency, by a smaller step each time in a growth day and by at most 0.12 in one growth day, so one afternoon cannot teach it. From proficiency 0.8 the page calls the trick learned. With no practice it fades toward 0.15 (time constant 12 growth days), never to nothing. Fear and sleepiness lower the chance.

| Verb | Kind | Name | Say | Claims | Runs on | Growth day | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sit` | built in | Sit | “sit”, “sit down”, “take a seat” | `sit_down` Sit down | Sit-stand policy (Pollen v5) | 0 | Gives up after 8 s. |
| `stand` | built in | Stand up | “stand”, “stand up”, “get up” | `stand_up` Stand up | Sit-stand policy (Pollen v5) | 0 | Gives up after 8 s. |
| `come` | built in | Come | “come”, “come here”, “come to me” | `follow` Follow along | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | 5 | Gives up after 15 s. `come` and `follow` both claim `follow`. |
| `look_at_me` | built in | Look at me | “look at me”, “look here”, “watch me” | `watch` Watch closely | Brain program on the standing or sit-stand policy | 0 | Gives up after 6 s. |
| `stop` | built in | Stop | “stop”, “halt”, “freeze” | `freeze` Freeze and stare | Brain program, plus trained skills (families: `freeze`) | 0 | Gives up after 5 s. |
| `follow` | built in | Follow me | “follow me”, “follow”, “come with me” | `follow` Follow along | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | 5 | Follows for 20 s. `follow` and `come` both claim `follow`. |
| `go_home` | built in | Go home | “go home”, “go to your nest”, “go to your dock” | `return_dock` Go back to charge | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | 5 | Gives up after 120 s. |
| `lie_down` | trick | Lie down | “lie down”, “lay down”, “take a nap” | `lie_low` Lie low for a moment | Trained skill `lie_low` | 5 | Gives up after 12 s. It lies low for a moment (the `lie_low` act). It is not sleep. Praise within 3 s of `peekaboo` (the same act done by itself) also teaches it. |
| `spin` | trick | Spin | “spin”, “turn around”, “twirl” | `spin` Spin | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | 5 | Gives up after 10 s. Done once its own odometry says it went once round. Not on a low battery or in the dark. |
| `bow` | trick | Bow | “bow”, “take a bow”, “curtsy” | `bow` Bow | Trained skill `bow` | 5 | Gives up after 8 s. The same bow it makes when it greets someone. Praise within 3 s of `greet` (the same act done by itself) also teaches it. |
| `shake` | trick | Shake | “shake”, “shake it off”, “shake off” | `body_shake` Shake it off | Trained skill `shake_1`, `shake_2` | 5 | Gives up after 8 s. The same shake-off it does by itself. |
| `flip` | trick | Flip | “flip”, “do a flip”, “somersault” | `flip` Flip | Trained skill `roulade` | 45 | Gives up after 25 s. Only standing, calm and upright for 1.5 s, with nothing solid 0.6 m ahead or 0.3 m all around, and a battery of at least 50%. At most 4 an hour, 120 s apart. It never starts from sitting. |
| `go_there` | pointed | Go there | Point at the floor on the page (experimental). | `wander` with the place as its goal | Walking policy (Pollen v5 `velstand`) | 5 | Gives up when stuck or out of time (45 s plus 15 s per metre). A place farther than 12 m is not an errand. |

## 7. Autonomous behaviours

Everything else the brain does. The brain keeps a list of wants (drives, senses, habits) that pull on each act; the strongest wins and it keeps going until it is satisfied. Acts are grouped by family. `bow`, `lie_low`, `spin`, `flip` have no wants of their own: only a command (a trick, section 6) starts them.
